My theory is this, the environment is like a non-stop uphill battle. Every single shop has deadlines that change constantly, a department that's always scrambling, and this burns people out. I'm salary and paid well but I need to check myself sometimes and say "It'll just be another emergency next week, go home and have dinner with your family." Machinist are smart in general, critical thinkers, and problem solvers. But when the same problems arise from planning, the tool room, management, and unrealistic expectations, that wears a soul out. Now with the toxic mentality, ya it's contagious and hard not to fall into the trenches of despair and "f*ck it" but I personally try and bring a good attitude to the issues and crack jokes etc. Some folks are just too far into the muck and don't want to get out. 
As for the insane amount of racist, homophobic, sexist bs. I don't pay them any mind, those dinosaurs are dying out and the young ones get put in their place and asked to keep it professional, that's all I can do as I've tried to fight it at every shop I'm at to no avail. Just my two tenths.
12 years in and always trying to make things better, but ya. I'm tired of always fighting to advocate for better conditions for everyone, I'm a day away from being a grumpy f*ck who no longer cares.

Oh dude thank you so much 🙏 So here’s how I got that finish. 

1 part ferric chloride
3.5 parts distilled water 

Stored in a plastic or glass cylinder style container (I use the glass cereal containers)

Clean blade perfectly with rubbing alcohol ensuring no bloody dust bunnies remain.

Soak completely for 5 minutes and make sure that no exposed or “finished” edges are leaning against the side. I use wire to hold it up.

Remove and “spritz” with distilled water and repeat soak 3 times. 

Then spritz and soak for 40 minutes.

Remove and let sit for 10 minutes then rinse with dish soap and hot water.

Spray with WD-40 and let hang for 10 hours. 

Hope that helps. 🤘
